quarterly_data.signal: At the TSMC 2026 North America Open Innovation Platform (OIP) Ecosystem Forum, Alchip presented a technical paper with Synopsys on how AI data center ASICs can overcome scale-up and scale-out bandwidth constraints, combining Synopsys 224G PHY IP with Alchip's advanced packaging and signal/power integrity (SI/PI) expertise in a protocol-agnostic physical design. At 224 Gbps SerDes speeds the work co-optimized escape routing, die-edge utilization (differentiated East/West vs North/South die edges) and package-substrate breakout; it extended to E/W package breakout techniques to sustain 1.6 terabits per second of networking bandwidth, and the approach is described as forward-scalable to ultimately support 448G SerDes. Alchip says engineers achieved chip-to-chip interconnect bandwidth density approaching theoretical physical limits, demonstrating the feasibility of ultra high density 224G scale-up interconnect. A technical paper / methodology, not a product launch or design win; no customers or dates stated.
quarterly_data.figure: Synopsys 224G PHY IP + Alchip packaging/SI-PI; 1.6 terabits per second E/W package breakout; scalable to 448G SerDes

By region, North America 51%, Asia Pacific 25%, Japan and the rest of the world 24%. Gross profit was $84.2 million (up 36.7% YoY, 26.8% QoQ) and pre-tax profit $64.4 million (up 23.9% YoY, 14.2% QoQ).
quarterly_data.figure: 7nm and smaller 87% of Q2 revenue; 5nm/7nm 40%; 12nm and larger 13%; HPC and Niche 51%; Asia Pacific 25%; Japan and rest of world 24%; gross profit $84.2 million; pre-tax profit $64.4 million

contracts.signal: AWS Graviton (Arm-based) is the host CPU paired with Trainium3; per Arm, Amazon/Trainium are increasingly going 100% Arm

AWS announced plans to deploy TENS OF MILLIONS of Graviton5 cores to power agentic AI workloads. CEO Rene Haas cited Graviton5, at 192 CORES, as an Arm-based instance in the market with a greater number of cores than Arm's own 128-core AGI CPU, and said more cores is 'clearly the direction of travel' for agentic workloads because the software overhead is simpler and virtual machines or jobs on single cores are 'much more efficient in terms of throughput'.
contracts.units: tens of millions of Graviton5 cores (192 cores per CPU)

quarterly_data.signal: Arm data-center royalty more than doubled YoY again, with Amazon/Graviton named among the deployments driving cloud-AI overperformance; Neoverse shipments have passed 1.5 billion cores (most recent 500 million in nine months). AWS plans tens of millions of Graviton5 cores for agentic AI workloads.
